Full layouts of scheduler, per-shard, mask-reference, task-iterator, runqueue and task extension objects.
Semantics of arena init, shard allocation, scheduler linkage, sysfs add, bypass, capability seeding, dispatch-one and effective-capability sync.
Operation table layout, operation indices, attach arguments, exit reasons and error sanitization rules.

findings.text: Sub-scheduler bring-up tail performs ordered initialization: arena pool, per-shard capability storage, scheduler linkage, sysfs exposure, nesting depth check, kernel arena objects, optional scheduler init operation, parent attach handshake, bypass engagement, operation presence bitmap construction, cgroup subtree claim, two-phase task adoption, bypass release, owed capability seeding, log and uevent announcement, with centralized failure path that records an error and schedules teardown.

Task adoption uses a temporary per-task marker over two sweeps. First sweep initializes each unmarked task for the child while it remains assigned to the parent, marking success. Second sweep moves marked tasks from parent to child, disabling and exiting from parent then assigning and enabling on child when on the extension class, clearing the marker to suppress duplicate visits.

Enable abort unwinds only initialization: it re-sweeps the subtree, cancels child initialization for marked tasks and clears the marker, without invoking disable callbacks that would lack a matching enable. A global enabling pointer stays set until all markers are cleared so concurrent exiting paths can exit for both parent and child.

Child enable claims cgroups before tasks, assigns the subtree root to the child, verifies online status, and requires every visited task to be in ready or enabled condition before transition. Non-extension tasks may remain ready under partial switching roots and become enabled later on class switch.

Child enable enforces maximum nesting depth, runs scheduler init before parent attach, marks initialized state on success, requires parent acceptance before proceeding, engages bypass during mutation, derives operation presence bits from non-null operation slots, and seeds capabilities owed since attach only after the child is fully enabled.

Cgroup task migration is split into three phases: preparing phase initializes the task for the destination scheduler, completion phase rehomes it under runqueue lock, cancellation phase discards the prepared initialization. Each phase is a no-op when cgroup support is off or the task is already on the destination.

Cgroup lifetime handling inherits scheduler association from parent on online for default hierarchy groups, and shuts down a scheduler whose own group goes offline with a cgroup-offline reason. Initialization registers lifetime and task-migration notifiers on the corresponding chains.

Dispatch helper lets a parent scheduler invoke dispatching for a child identified by cgroup identifier in locked runqueue context. It rejects unknown children, rejects non-direct children with an error, skips children lacking effective base capability on the current processor, and reports whether dispatch produced work.

Capability helper preamble resolves the calling scheduler from program metadata, requires cid-form operation, resolves the target child by cgroup identifier, requires a direct parent-child link, and rejects capability bits outside the allowed set.

Grant interface allows a parent to offer a set of capabilities over a caller-supplied cid mask to a direct child, shard by shard, optionally collecting rejected cids into a caller-supplied mask. It grants a cid only when the parent holds every requested capability there, delivers change notifications after all shards, and signals partial denial distinctly from full success.

Grant is all-or-nothing per cid within a shard: requested bits are intersected with parent holdings to form the grantable set, child storage is updated only with newly set cids, per-cid effective-capability synchronization is queued for changed cids, and change records are batched then delivered once.

Revoke interface clears a set of capabilities over a caller-supplied cid mask from a child subtree. It walks descendants in pre-order under shard locks, records changes and queues effective-capability synchronization for affected cids, skips a subtree when its root lost nothing, and delivers notifications after all shards.

Capability query reads the union of requested capability holdings for self when the identifier is zero, otherwise for a direct child. It validates the capability mask and output mask, requires capability storage to be published, and copies one per-shard union per shard into the caller output.

Capability query tolerates early self-reads during initialization by checking published storage with acquire ordering; unpublished storage is reported as unavailable rather than dereferenced. Shard range metadata is read under read-side protection.
Child termination helper lets a parent shut down a direct child with a parent-kill exit reason and caller-formatted message. It requires cid-form operation and rejects unknown or non-direct targets.
Fallback variants for non-cid builds report operation-not-supported for grant, query and kill, and perform no action for revoke.

Reentry detectors report scheduler errors naming dispatch and capability-update operations when the same program reenters those paths. Lookup of the scheduler from program metadata is read-side protected and silently ignores programs with no scheduler.
Cgroup path helper returns the scheduler-associated path in the enabled configuration and a fixed root path in the alternate configuration.

Child enable holds the enable mutex across the whole sequence, uses CPUs read protection for kernel arena allocation, holds fork write protection plus cgroup lock across subtree claim and task sweeps with temporary iterator release around per-task initialization, and uses runqueue locking for per-task state checks and marker updates plus scheduler-change protection for the parent-to-child move.

Grant and revoke run with interrupts saved, take one parent shard lock then nested child or descendant shard locks in shard order, and defer notification delivery until after locks are released. Query runs with interrupts saved and relies on published-storage ordering plus read-side protection for shard ranges.

Dispatch, kill and reentry paths use read-side protection for scheduler lookup. Task migration completion and cancellation use runqueue locking for rehome and cancel. Preparing migration performs initialization without holding runqueue lock.

Cpu-id mask carries a base identifier, a count of covered identifiers, a count of allocated words, and a trailing flexible array of bit words. A helper macro declares a stack mask slice for one shard with a caller base and count bounded by the per-shard processor limit.
Shard descriptor carries a base cid and a count of cids in that shard.
Topology descriptor carries paired identifier and index values for core, last-level cache, node and shard levels.

Scheduler limits observed as facts: maximum sub-scheduler nesting depth is four; default dispatch batch and maximum dispatch loops are thirty-two each; task iterator batch is thirty-two; per-CPU task identifier chunk is one thousand twenty-four; reenqueue repeat limit is two hundred fifty-six; bypass host stride is two; bypass load-balance batch is two hundred fifty-six.

Rescue and watchdog facts: watchdog maximum timeout is thirty times the clock tick rate; rescue default bandwidth is twenty parts per thousand, maximum two hundred fifty, disable sentinel is the maximum unsigned thirty-two-bit value; rescue quantum default five thousand microseconds with minimum one thousand and maximum one hundred thousand; rescue slice floor one thousand microseconds; overload multiplier sixteen; overload window minimum one thousand milliseconds and maximum fifteen thousand milliseconds.

Exit, capacity, bypass-interval and cid-shard facts: exit backtrace length sixty-four, message length one thousand twenty-four, default dump length thirty-two thousand seven hundred sixty-eight; capacity unit equals the scheduler capacity scale; bypass load-balance default interval is five hundred milliseconds, donor percentage one hundred twenty-five, minimum delta divisor four; default cid shard size twenty-four and maximum cpus per shard five hundred twelve.

Task iteration may visit the same task twice when racing exit, so marker set and clear are used to skip duplicates. A task may die between initialization and runqueue locking; that path cancels the just-completed child initialization instead of enabling. Tasks are reference-held across iterator release to keep them pinned.

Enable failures after partial bring-up must not leave bypass off or tasks half-owned: failure paths keep bypass engaged into teardown, record an error even when the failure returned only an errno, flush disable work, and suppress duplicate error handling by reporting success to the outer command after scheduling teardown.

Capability operations fail safely on invalid masks, unpublished storage, non-cid operation, unknown child, non-direct child, and capability bits outside the allowed set. Dispatch additionally refuses distant children and children without effective base capability, avoiding inserts that would be rejected.
